title: Epistemic authority and generative AI in learning spaces: rethinking knowledge in the algorithmic age
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the epistemological and pedagogical consequences of generative AI in learning spaces, focusing on how tools such as ChatGPT reshape what counts as knowledge, who is seen as authoritative, and how students and teachers relate to one another. Rather than evaluating a specific intervention, the article argues that generative AI can function as a “surrogate knower,” encouraging automation bias, weakening traditional norms of justification, and shifting epistemic authority away from human educators toward algorithmic outputs.

The authors discuss generative AI as embedded in classroom learning, feedback, and assessment contexts, but the paper itself is a conceptual/opinion piece rather than an empirical study. It draws on prior literature and philosophical framing to describe how AI-generated outputs may reinforce dominant discourses, reproduce bias, and operate as a hidden curriculum that privileges fluency, certainty, and speed over critical reflection and pluralistic inquiry. The article also highlights the potential for AI use by both students and instructors to blur teacher-student boundaries and alter perceptions of expertise and objectivity.

The paper concludes by arguing for “epistemic agency” and a model of the teacher as an “epistemic mentor.” It recommends reflective pedagogies such as comparing AI responses with peer or instructor feedback, trust audits, journaling, source checking, and critical AI literacy. The central conclusion is that education should not simply adopt AI for efficiency, but should actively frame its use in ways that preserve human judgment, critical discernment, and democratic learning values.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generative AI / large language model chatbots used for producing and transforming text, answering questions, giving feedback, and supporting instruction.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper is an opinion/theoretical discussion about generative AI in learning spaces, with examples including ChatGPT and other large language models; it does not evaluate a specific tool in an empirical study.

quality_tier_rationale: This is an opinion/theoretical paper rather than an empirical controlled, quasi-controlled, or review study. It does not report a systematic methodology or original outcome data on any AI tool.
impact_tier_rationale: No causal or descriptive effect estimates are reported, so there is no measurable instructional or learning impact to rate.
